hypothesis.statement: The whole remaining residual is ONE mechanism -- which register holds base+off across the second loop, and therefore whether the CTLBLIT fields are reached at large displacements off a callee-saved base (target: r28 at +7644/+7648/+7660) or at small displacements off a separately formed pointer (ours: r29 at +4/+8). Five source forms across two lanes have failed to move it, and the +0x78 and +0x114 rows are symptoms of that one register web rather than independent levers. The untried framing is to attack the FIRST loop instead of the second: the target reuses one callee-saved register for base+off and then for the CTLBLIT pointer precisely because base+off is dead at that point, so a form that makes base+off provably dead earlier -- e.g. consuming it into the mbBlitCalcWidth argument before the CTLBLIT pointer is formed -- is the one shape nobody has written.
